updates.problem: Flat lineage labels and raw source counts can overstate corroboration when evidence shares remote datasets, analyses, intellectual ancestors, alternate IDs, or versions.
updates.result: A frozen provenance DAG contract now detects known shared ancestry, collapses alternate identities, propagates unknown ancestry, rejects invalid graph structure, exposes structural provenance components, and can only preserve or downgrade generator-family corroboration. It explicitly refuses to infer statistical/epistemic independence or numeric effective N from graph topology.
updates.remaining_gap: Real scientific duplicated-ancestry utility is untested. Compare raw count, flat labels and explicit lineage graph on a frozen real corpus under matched model/resource/evaluator budgets.
updates.falsifier: If graph-aware lineage analysis does not reduce false corroboration or improve failure localization versus simpler baselines, keep provenance for audit only and do not activate extra decision-layer complexity.

updates.note: Include explicit shared-data/derivation ancestry cases so generator-family corroboration is evaluated with lineage-aware support rather than raw source count.
Round 029 adds evidence-to-evidence ancestry support, not the still-open exact claim-span-to-evidence provenance contract. Do not conflate these fibers.
A deterministic compiler remains needed to reconstruct all fiber definitions/statuses and detect future orphan/conflicting references.

saturation.reason: Round 029 retained a new typed provenance-dependence contract and generator-family downgrade semantics after semantic deduplication.
